message.content:
Use the identity \(\cos 4x=\sin(90^\circ-4x)\):

\[
\sin 6x+\cos 4x=0
\]

\[
\sin 6x+\sin(90^\circ-4x)=0
\]

Using sum-to-product,

\[
2\sin\left(\frac{6x+90^\circ-4x}{2}\right)\cos\left(\frac{6x-(90^\circ-4x)}{2}\right)=0
\]

\[
2\sin(x+45^\circ)\cos(5x-45^\circ)=0
\]

So either:

\[
\sin(x+45^\circ)=0
\]

Since \(0^\circ\le x<180^\circ\), this gives

\[
x+45^\circ=180^\circ \implies x=135^\circ
\]

Or:

\[
\cos(5x-45^\circ)=0
\]

\[
5x-45^\circ=90^\circ+180^\circ k
\]

\[
5x=135^\circ+180^\circ k
\]

\[
x=27^\circ+36^\circ k
\]

For \(0^\circ\le x<180^\circ\):

\[
x=27^\circ,63^\circ,99^\circ,135^\circ,171^\circ
\]

The answer is \(27^\circ, 63^\circ, 99^\circ, 135^\circ, 171^\circ\).
